headline: Centrus Energy's HALEU Monopoly Meets Palantir as Nuclear Demand Builds
lede: Centrus Energy (LEU) occupies a singular position in American energy: its American Centrifuge Plant in Piketon, Ohio is the only facility in the Western world currently licensed and actively enriching uranium to *HALEU* grade, the fuel required by most next-generation reactor designs. A March 2026 software partnership with Palantir Technologies has renewed retail interest in the stock, which sits roughly 52 percent below its October 2025 peak. The bull case rests on a $3.9 billion backlog, a fresh $900 million Department of Energy expansion contract, and the argument that demand for advanced reactor fuel will eventually overwhelm available supply.
body:
Centrus Energy (LEU), formerly USEC Inc., operates the **American Centrifuge Plant** in Piketon, Ohio — the only facility in the United States, and the Western world, licensed by the *Nuclear Regulatory Commission* to produce *HALEU*: uranium enriched to between 5% and 20% U-235. Conventional reactors use fuel enriched to roughly 3–5%; advanced designs — *small modular reactors*, microreactors, and Generation IV concepts — need the higher grade to achieve smaller geometries, longer operating cycles, and higher thermal efficiency. As of mid-2026, Centrus has delivered over 920 kilograms of HALEU to the Department of Energy, a modest fraction of the agency's projected domestic need of 50 metric tonnes per year by 2035.

In January 2026, the DOE awarded Centrus a $900 million base task order — rising to $1.07 billion with options — to expand Piketon to commercial-scale HALEU production, with first new capacity expected by 2029. Full-year 2024 revenue came in at $442 million, up 38 percent year-over-year, with net income of $73.2 million. The Q1 2026 picture was murkier: GAAP net income fell 63 percent versus the prior year, weighed down by rising expansion costs, though the company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $450–$500 million and reported a $3.9 billion utility-contract backlog stretching to 2040.

The detail attracting retail attention is a March 2026 partnership with Palantir Technologies (PLTR). Centrus is deploying Palantir's *Foundry* data-integration platform and its *AIP* across the Piketon expansion — covering project controls, supply-chain management, manufacturing execution, and regulatory compliance. The company announced it had identified “nearly $300 million in savings” within the first six weeks of deployment. That figure warrants scrutiny: it represents projected reductions in the cost of a multi-billion-dollar construction program, not cuts to the existing operating budget, and it carries no public methodology or independent verification. CEO Amir Vexler called it “only the beginning,” a framing that analysts at Evercore ISI (EVR) described as positive for execution de-risking without endorsing the specific number.

The stock reached an all-time high of roughly $440–$464 in October 2025 before retreating to around $207 by May 2026 — a drawdown exceeding 50 percent. Short interest stands at approximately 23.5 percent of the float, meaningfully elevated and consistent with a market skeptical of the expansion timeline and unit economics, but not at the extreme levels that would imply forced covering on any modest positive catalyst.

The “only U.S. licensed producer” framing will not hold indefinitely. The same January 2026 DOE award that fortified Centrus also extended comparable $900 million task orders to General Matter — building enrichment capacity at the former Paducah, Kentucky site, targeting 2034 operations — and to Orano Federal Services, the U.S. arm of the French state-controlled Orano group. Urenco USA, the sole other commercially operating enricher in the country, produces conventional low-enriched uranium for existing reactors and does not yet hold an HALEU license. Whether Centrus can translate its first-mover advantage and institutional DOE relationship into durable commercial dominance before competitors come online is the question the market has not resolved.

concepts.definition: High-Assay Low-Enriched Uranium: uranium enriched to between 5% and 20% U-235, distinguishing it from conventional reactor fuel (3–5%) and weapons-grade material (90%+). Most advanced and next-generation reactor designs require HALEU because its higher energy density enables smaller, longer-lived core designs that cannot run on conventional fuel.

A uranium enrichment facility in Piketon, Ohio, operated by Centrus Energy's subsidiary American Centrifuge Operating. It uses gas centrifuge technology — spinning uranium hexafluoride at high speed to separate heavier U-238 from lighter U-235 — and is the only facility in the Western world currently licensed and actively producing HALEU.

The U.S. federal agency that licenses and oversees civilian nuclear facilities, including uranium enrichment plants. An NRC license is required before any facility can legally produce enriched uranium on American soil; Centrus received its HALEU-specific license amendment in June 2021.

A nuclear reactor design with an electrical output typically below 300 megawatts — far smaller than conventional gigawatt-scale plants. SMRs are designed for factory fabrication and modular deployment; most advanced designs require HALEU fuel rather than the conventional low-enriched uranium used in today's light-water reactors.

Palantir Technologies' enterprise data-integration and operations platform. It creates a unified data layer — called an ontology — across an organization's disparate systems, enabling analytics, workflow automation, and AI-model deployment on top of real operational data.

Palantir's Artificial Intelligence Platform, a layer built on top of Foundry that enables large-language-model and machine-learning applications to act directly on enterprise operational data. In manufacturing and construction contexts it is used for predictive cost modeling, supply-chain optimization, and schedule compression.

The percentage of a company's tradable shares (the float) that investors have borrowed and sold short, betting the price will fall. Elevated short interest — above roughly 15–20% of float — can amplify upward price moves if positive news forces short-sellers to buy back shares quickly, a dynamic sometimes called a short squeeze.

In the nuclear fuel industry, the total dollar value of signed customer purchase contracts for future delivery of uranium fuel or enrichment services. A large, long-dated backlog indicates revenue visibility years into the future and significantly reduces near-term execution risk for investors.

fact_check: The tweet's claim that Palantir is 'saving over $300M in costs' is misleading as stated. The figure represents projected savings on the multi-billion-dollar Piketon construction and expansion project — identified within six weeks of deploying Palantir's software — not reductions to the company's existing operating cost base. No independent methodology or third-party verification has been published; the number comes entirely from Centrus's own press release. The claim that Centrus is the 'only U.S. licensed producer/supplier of HALEU' is accurate as of mid-2026 for active production, but the January 2026 DOE award also gives comparable task orders to General Matter and Orano Federal Services, both of which are building competing enrichment capacity. The 'good recent earnings' characterization applies to full-year 2024 (revenue +38%, net income $73.2M) but overstates Q1 2026, when GAAP net income fell 63% year-over-year and the stock dropped 8.8% in a single session on the release.
